data.narrative:
Terran Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zach Dwiel and Danny Weddle that has raised $256K to date. The relevant peer universe comprises one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms in robotics and manufacturing, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

Given the company's early stage and limited funding history, peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables; only one same-stage peer existed within the robotics sector, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold needed for robust triangulation. Stage-progression methodology was therefore the primary valuation approach. Applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $256K base value yielded an implied valuation of $640K.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $544K to $736K, centered on $640K. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific sector and founder profile, and the absence of granular financial or traction metrics in the dataset. A more refined range would require additional comparables at seed and Series A stages within robotics, or disclosure of current revenue, user adoption, or technology differentiation.
